problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{6}{{s}^{2}-6s}.$

feedback.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}-9}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we write $F(s)$ as a sum of partial fractions, as follows: 

$$
\frac{1}{{s}^{2}-9}=\frac{1}{(s-3)(s+3)}=\frac{1}{6(s-3)}-\frac{1}{6(s+3)}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{3t}} & =\frac{1}{s-3},\,s>3 \\ L{{e}^{-3t}} & =\frac{1}{s+3},\,s>-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition property of the Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{6(s-3)}-\frac{1}{6(s+3)}} & =\frac{1}{6}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-3}}-\frac{1}{6}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{6}{e}^{-3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}-9}$ is $f(t)=\frac{1}{6}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{6}{e}^{-3t}.$
